Build money-flow (Sankey) data from PEIMS finance rows

txs_peims_flow.Rd

Aggregates a txs_get_peims_finance() result (typically filtered to one district) into the stage-to-stage edge list behind an income-statement-style flow diagram: where the money came from, which fund it moved through, and what it was spent on. Plot the result with txs_plot_peims_flow() or any Sankey tool.

Usage

txs_peims_flow(x, axes = c("source", "fund", "function"), lump = 5)

Arguments

x

A tibble from txs_get_peims_finance() (tidy output), usually filtered to one district and year.

axes

Character vector of two or more axes from the list above, in canonical order.

lump

Maximum number of nodes per axis before smaller ones fold into an "Other ..." node (balance nodes excepted).

Value

A tibble of class peims_flow with columns from_axis, from, to_axis, to, amount, carrying the axis vector as an attribute.

Axes and honesty

Available axes, in canonical order:

  • "source" – revenue class from the object code: local (5700s), state (5800s), federal (5900s).

  • "fund" – TEA fund (general fund, food service, Title I, ...).

  • "function" – what the spending was for (instruction, ...).

  • "object" – what was bought: payroll (6100s), contracted services (6200s), supplies (6300s), other operating (6400s), debt service (6500s), capital outlay (6600s).

  • "program" – program intent (basic, special education, ...).

Every edge is a genuine total from the data: revenue rows record (source, fund) jointly, and expenditure rows record (fund, function, object, program) jointly. Because TEA does not record which revenue dollar paid which bill, "source" may only be followed by "fund" (money is only traceable source-to-spending through a fund); requesting e.g. c("source", "function") errors.

Transfers, proceeds, and fund balances

When axes starts at "source", the flow uses everything PEIMS records about a fund's two sides:

  • ordinary revenues (objects 5700-5900) enter by source class;

  • inter-fund transfers (objects 7915 in / 8911 out) enter from a "Transfers from other funds" node and leave to a "Transfers to other funds" node. PEIMS records each end on its own fund but not the fund-to-fund pairing, so transfers are drawn as half-edges through those nodes rather than as invented fund-to-fund ribbons;

  • other financing sources and uses (remaining 7900s/8900s: bond, loan, and lease proceeds, asset sales, ...) enter from an "Other financing sources" node and leave to an "Other financing uses" node;

  • what remains is the genuine change in the fund's pot: each fund's shortfall is fed by a "From fund balance" node and each fund's surplus drains to a "To fund balance" node, so both sides of every fund reconcile exactly.

Without a "source" axis (spending-side charts), only expenditure rows (6000s) are drawn and the 7000s/8000s are omitted.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
txs_get_peims_finance(2024, "actual", "district") |>
  dplyr::filter(district == "161920") |>
  txs_peims_flow() |>
  txs_plot_peims_flow()
} # }
